title: Trojan War — Comparative mythology
summary: The Trojan War was fought over Helen, lasting ten years and ending with the wooden horse. This study sets the myth beside its cousins worldwide.
body:
The Trojan War was fought over Helen, lasting ten years and ending with the wooden horse. Homer's Iliad covers only a few weeks of its final year.

Floods, tricksters, dying gods, world trees — the same patterns recur across continents. Setting Trojan War beside its parallels tests whether the pattern is human nature, cultural diffusion, or coincidence. Viewed through a symbolic lens, Trojan War is read for its images — what each figure and object stands for beneath the plot.

Comparison honors Trojan War by taking it seriously as one answer among many. A fourth sub-question examines the moral the myth was meant to teach its first hearers. Related entries in this archive: Bifrost and Ziggurats.
